judged_text: The helper's return value is a union of a raw fetch Response (sharing branch) and whatever the provider-specific refreshFunction returns, with refreshFunction typed `() => any`, so TypeScript cannot flag call sites that consume the two branches differently. Four call sites (google, hubspot, zoho-bigin, zohocrm) compiled while reading token fields or .data off a fetch Response; the next app converted to this helper will repeat the same mistake unless the two branches are split into separately-typed functions.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` in the sharing branch, but returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns in the normal branch (typed `() => any`). Several updated call sites assume the returned value has provider-specific shapes like `.data` (Axios/Gaxios) or token fields: e.g. Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, Zoho Bigin checks `tokenInfo.data.error`, and Zoho CRM checks `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. If `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, these will receive a `Response` object (no `.data`), causing broken behavior at runtime, and TypeScript won’t catch it due to `any`/union behavior.
